claim: Photo-transduction in cone segments (CS) is crucial for high acuity daytime vision.
source: Photo-transduction in cone segments (CS) is crucial for high acuity daytime vision.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about cone segment function.

claim: Cone segments degenerate in retinitis pigmentosa (RP) for ill-defined reasons.
source: For ill-defined reasons, CS degenerate in retinitis pigmentosa (RP)
evidence: This statement acknowledges the observation of CS degeneration in RP while noting the mechanism is not well understood.

claim: Cone segments degenerate in the transitional zone (TZ) of atrophic zones (AZ) which characterize geographic atrophy (GA).
source: For ill-defined reasons, CS degenerate in retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and in the transitional zone (TZ) of atrophic zones (AZ), which characterize geographic atrophy (GA).
evidence: This statement describes a clinical observation about CS degeneration in GA.

claim: Cone segments are lost in the TZ of patients with GA.
source: Our experiments confirm the loss of cone segments (CS) in the TZ of patients with GA
evidence: The authors present experimental data from human donor eyes showing CS loss in the TZ.

claim: Cone segment loss in the TZ is associated with subretinal CD14+ mononuclear phagocyte (MP) infiltration.
source: Our experiments confirm the loss of cone segments (CS) in the TZ of patients with GA and show their association with subretinal CD14+mononuclear phagocyte (MP) infiltration
evidence: The authors present immunohistochemical data showing co-localization of CS loss and CD14+ MPs.

claim: Subretinal CD14+ mononuclear phagocyte infiltration is reported in RP.
source: show their association with subretinal CD14+mononuclear phagocyte (MP) infiltration that is also reported in RP.
evidence: This refers to published literature on MP infiltration in RP.

claim: MP-derived IL-1β leads to severe CS degeneration in human and mouse MPs in vitro.
source: Using human and mouse MPs in vitro and inflammation-prone Cx3cr1GFP/GFP mice in vivo, we demonstrate that MP-derived IL-1β leads to severe CS degeneration.
evidence: The authors present experimental data from co-culture experiments showing IL-1β-dependent CS degeneration.

claim: MP-derived IL-1β leads to severe CS degeneration in inflammation-prone Cx3cr1GFP/GFP mice in vivo.
source: Using human and mouse MPs in vitro and inflammation-prone Cx3cr1GFP/GFP mice in vivo, we demonstrate that MP-derived IL-1β leads to severe CS degeneration.
evidence: The authors present experimental data from light-challenged mice showing IL-1β-dependent CS degeneration.

claim: Subretinal MP accumulation participates in pathological photoreceptor changes in GA and RP.
source: Our results strongly suggest that subretinal MP accumulation participates in the observed pathological photoreceptor changes in these diseases.
evidence: This is an inference based on the association observed in human samples and the experimental results in vitro and in vivo.

claim: Inhibiting subretinal MP accumulation might protect cone segments and help preserve high acuity daytime vision in conditions characterized by subretinal inflammation.
source: Inhibiting subretinal MP accumulation or Il-1β might protect the CS and help preserve high acuity daytime vision in conditions characterized by subretinal inflammation, such as AMD and RP.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic suggestion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Inhibiting IL-1β might protect cone segments and help preserve high acuity daytime vision in conditions characterized by subretinal inflammation.
source: Inhibiting subretinal MP accumulation or Il-1β might protect the CS and help preserve high acuity daytime vision in conditions characterized by subretinal inflammation, such as AMD and RP.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic suggestion based on the experimental findings showing IL-1β inhibition prevents CS loss.

claim: The macula consists of a small cone-dominated fovea responsible for high acuity vision.
source: The macula consists of a small cone-dominated fovea, responsible for high acuity vision, surrounded by a rod-dominated parafovea and peripheral retina.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about retinal structure.

claim: The fovea is surrounded by a rod-dominated parafovea and peripheral retina.
source: The macula consists of a small cone-dominated fovea, responsible for high acuity vision, surrounded by a rod-dominated parafovea and peripheral retina.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about retinal structure.

claim: Photo-transduction in cone segments is crucial for cone function and therefore high acuity and daytime vision.
source: Photo-transduction in cone segments (CS) are crucial for cone function and therefore high acuity and daytime vision.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cone physiology.

claim: Geographic atrophy is a late form of age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD).
source: In geographic atrophy (GA), a late form of age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD)
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about AMD classification.

claim: Geographic atrophy is characterized by an extending atrophic zone with loss of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and degeneration of the photoreceptor cell layer.
source: In geographic atrophy (GA), a late form of age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD), an extending atrophic zone (AZ) forms, characterized by the loss of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE, a monolayer of cells with important functions in photoreceptor homeostasis) and degeneration of the photoreceptor cell layer (Sarks, 1976).
evidence: This is a cited description of GA pathology.

claim: The RPE is a monolayer of cells with important functions in photoreceptor homeostasis.
source: the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE, a monolayer of cells with important functions in photoreceptor homeostasis)
evidence: This is established knowledge about RPE structure and function.

claim: The initial lesion in GA often develops parafoveally.
source: The initial lesion in GA often develops parafoveally (Sarks et al., 1988)
evidence: This is a cited observation about GA progression.

claim: The GA lesion slowly expands through the central retina and fovea, which leads to a severe drop in visual acuity.
source: The initial lesion in GA often develops parafoveally (Sarks et al., 1988) and slowly expands through the central retina and fovea, which leads to a severe drop in visual acuity.
evidence: This is cited knowledge about GA progression and its clinical consequences.

claim: In the atrophic zone, despite the absence of the RPE, residual cones survive but lack cone segments.
source: In the AZ, despite the absence of the RPE, residual cones survive, but they lack the cone segments (CS) (Bird et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited observation from histological studies.

claim: Similar findings of residual cones lacking cone segments are observed in disciform subretinal scars, the end-stage of exudative AMD.
source: Similar findings are observed in disciform subretinal scars, the end-stage of exudative AMD (Curcio, 2001).
evidence: This is a cited observation from histological studies.

claim: In the transitional zone just peripheral to the RPE-loss in the scar and AZ, the number of rods drops dramatically compared to the retina more distant from the lesion.
source: Surprisingly, in a transitional zone (TZ), just peripheral to the RPE-loss in the scar and AZ, the number of rods drops dramatically compared to the retina more distant from the lesion (Bird et al., 2014; Curcio, 2001).
evidence: This is a cited observation from histological studies.

claim: In the transitional zone, the number of cones changes little, but they lack their cone segments.
source: In contrast, the number of cones changes little in the TZ, but they lack their CS (Bird et al., 2014; Curcio, 2001).
evidence: This is a cited observation from histological studies.

claim: CS loss is observed in retinitis pigmentosa (RP) patients with rod-gene mutations and unremarkable RPE.
source: One could assume that the CS loss in the TZ of AMD patients is due to RPE dysfunction, but CS loss is also observed in retinitis pigmentosa (RP) patients with rod-gene mutations and unremarkable RPE (Mitamura et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a cited observation that argues against RPE dysfunction as the sole cause of CS loss.

claim: Mononuclear phagocytes (MP) comprise a family of cells that include classical monocytes (Mo), macrophages (Mϕ), and microglial cells (MC) among others.
source: Mononuclear phagocytes (MP) comprise a family of cells that include classical monocytes (Mo), macrophages (Mϕ), and microglial cells (MC) among others (Chow et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a cited definition of mononuclear phagocytes.

claim: Subretinal MPs accumulate in the AZ and on the apical side of the RPE of the TZ in patients with GA.
source: We and others have shown that subretinal MPs accumulate in the AZ and on the apical side of the RPE of the TZ in patients with GA (Combadière et al., 2007; Gupta et al., 2003; Lad et al., 2015; Levy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited observation from multiple studies including the authors' own work.

claim: Numerous blood-derived MPs (CCR2-positive) invariably participate in the infiltration of both the AZ and TZ.
source: We have recently demonstrated that numerous blood-derived MPs (CCR2-positive) invariably participate in the infiltration of both, the AZ and TZ (Sennlaub et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a cited observation from the authors' previous work.

claim: The recruitment of blood-derived monocytes contributes importantly to autoimmune, photo-oxidative, and genetic photoreceptor degeneration in mice.
source: In mice, the recruitment of blood-derived monocytes contributes importantly to autoimmune, photo-oxidative, and genetic photoreceptor degeneration (Rutar et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2012; Kohno et al., 2013; Cruz-Guilloty, 2013)
evidence: This is a cited observation from multiple mouse studies.

claim: Bone-marrow derived murine monocytes induce rod apoptosis in vivo and in vitro.
source: we demonstrated that bone-marrow derived murine monocytes induce rod apoptosis in vivo and in vitro (Sennlaub et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a cited observation from the authors' previous work.

claim: Monocyte-induced rod apoptosis is in part mediated by IL-1β.
source: we demonstrated that bone-marrow derived murine monocytes induce rod apoptosis in vivo and in vitro (Sennlaub et al., 2013), which is in part mediated by IL-1β (Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited observation from the authors' previous work.

claim: Subretinal MPs accumulate in RP secondarily to primary rod cell death.
source: Interestingly, subretinal MPs also accumulate in RP secondarily to primary rod cell death
evidence: This is a cited observation about the sequence of events in RP.

claim: Subretinal MPs have been suggested to induce the unexplained CS degeneration in RP patients.
source: subretinal MPs also accumulate in RP secondarily to primary rod cell death, and have been suggested to induce the unexplained CS degeneration in these patients (Gupta et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a cited hypothesis from previous work.

claim: The TZ is infiltrated by CD14+ MPs.
source: We here confirm that the TZ is infiltrated by CD14+MPs
evidence: The authors present immunohistochemical data showing CD14+ MPs in the TZ.

claim: Rod photoreceptors are lost in the TZ despite the presence of underlying RPE.
source: We here confirm that the TZ is infiltrated by CD14+MPs and that rod photoreceptors and cone segments are lost in the TZ despite the presence of underlying RPE.
evidence: The authors present histological data showing rod loss in the TZ with intact RPE.

claim: Cone segments are lost in the TZ despite the presence of underlying RPE.
source: We here confirm that the TZ is infiltrated by CD14+MPs and that rod photoreceptors and cone segments are lost in the TZ despite the presence of underlying RPE.
evidence: The authors present histological data showing CS loss in the TZ with intact RPE.

claim: MP derived IL-1β induces CS degeneration in addition to previously reported rod apoptosis.
source: we show that MP derived IL-1β induces CS degeneration additionally to previously reported rod apoptosis.
evidence: The authors present experimental data from co-cultures and in vivo experiments showing IL-1β-dependent CS degeneration.

claim: The presence of CD14+ MPs in the subretinal space participates in CS degeneration as they produce similar changes in vitro and in vivo.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that the presence of CD14+MPs in the subretinal space, not only observed in the TZ but also in patients with RP, participates in CS degeneration as they produce similar changes in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the association in human samples and the experimental results.

claim: Bird and colleagues analyzed the loss of outer nuclear layer (ONL) nuclei and cone outer segments in GA using histology and electron microscopy.
source: Bird and colleagues recently analyzed the loss of outer nuclear layer (ONL) nuclei and cone outer segments in GA using histology and electron microscopy (Bird et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a citation to previous work.

claim: Rod loss and cone outer segment degeneration occur peripheral to the margin of the RPE defect, in the transitional zone (TZ).
source: They reported that rod loss and cone outer segment degeneration occur peripheral to the margin of the RPE defect, in the transitional zone (TZ) (Bird et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited observation from previous work.

claim: In the central region of control eyes, cone arrestin-rhodopsin double labeling visualized a 4 to 6 nuclei thick ONL, with cone segments (CS) and dendrites clearly demarcated by the cone arrestin immunological staining.
source: In the central region of control eyes, cone arrestin (green staining) -rhodopsin (red staining) double labeling visualized a 4 to 6 nuclei thick ONL, with cone segments (CS) and dendrites clearly demarcated by the cone arrestin immunological staining (Figure 1A, Hoechst blue staining of nuclei, RPE autofluorescence orange).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The rod outer segments (OS) are strongly immunologically positive for rhodopsin staining.
source: The rod outer segments (OS) are strongly immunologically positive for rhodopsin staining, while the rod cell bodies stained more faintly, but enough to identify rod cell bodies (Figure 1A inset).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The retina distant (>1000 μm) from the RPE lesion in sections from donor eyes with GA was very similar to the control eyes.
source: The retina distant (>1000 μm) from the RPE lesion in sections from donor eyes with GA was very similar to the control eyes (Figure 1B), featuring clearly marked cone arrestin+ CS (Figure 1B inset).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In the TZ, close to the margin of the lesion but where RPE was still present, the ONL was irregular, thinned (around 2 nuclei of ONL), and cone and rod morphology was severely altered with the outer segments missing and the inner segments difficult to distinguish from the cell bodies.
source: In the TZ, close to the margin of the lesion but where RPE was still present, the ONL was irregular, thinned (around 2 nuclei of ONL), and cone and rod morphology was severely altered with the outer segments missing and the inner segments difficult to distinguish from the cell bodies (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The thinning and loss of segments was invariably found to extend peripherally to the margin of the RPE loss, into the TZ.
source: The thinning and loss of segments was invariably found to extend peripherally to the margin of the RPE loss, into the TZ (Figure 1C, the autofluorescent RPE is visible in the left part of the micrograph, the arrow depicts the margin of the RPE with the atrophic zone to the right).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The TZ, characterized by a thinned ONL in the presence of underlying RPE, was of variable length (200–800 μm) in the samples.
source: The TZ, characterized by a thinned ONL in the presence of underlying RPE, was of variable length (200–800 μm) in our samples similar to previous reports (Bird et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the authors' histological analysis.

claim: Within the AZ residual cone arrestin+ cones, but also rhodopsin+ rods were observed in all but one analyzed samples, but their distribution was irregular and all photoreceptors lacked their OS.
source: Within the AZ residual cone arrestin+ cones, but also rhodopsin+ rods were observed in all but one analyzed samples, but their distribution was irregular and all photoreceptors lacked their OS (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The cone density at a greater than 1000 μm distance from the RPE-denuded AZ was similar between control and GA eyes.
source: The cone density at a greater than 1000 μm distance from the RPE-denuded AZ, was similar between control and GA eyes.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the authors' histological analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In the atrophic zone the number of cone somata was significantly reduced to around half the numbers of controls.
source: In the atrophic zone the number of cone somata was significantly reduced to around half the numbers of controls (Figure 1E)
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the authors' histological analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The number of cone somata was not significantly different in the TZ (0–200 μm from the AZ) compared to controls.
source: and was not significantly different in the TZ (0–200 μm from the AZ, which is the TZ length invariably found in all donor eyes).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the authors' histological analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Rod cell counts revealed a slight decrease distant from the lesions, but a severe 90% reduction in the TZ compared to controls.
source: Rod cell counts, on the other hand, revealed a slight decrease distant from the lesions, but a severe 90% reduction in the TZ compared to controls (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the authors' histological analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In all but one atrophic zone, rhodopsin+ residual rods were detected.
source: Interestingly, in all but one atrophic zone we also detected rhodopsin+ residual rods.
evidence: This is a qualitative observation from the authors' histological analysis.

claim: The results confirm a severe rod cell loss in the TZ of patients with GA, where the RPE is still morphologically intact.
source: Taken together, our results confirm a severe rod cell loss in the TZ of patients with GA, where the RPE is still morphologically intact
evidence: This is a summary statement of the histological findings.

claim: The number of cone numbers was relatively spared in the TZ.
source: Taken together, our results confirm a severe rod cell loss in the TZ of patients with GA, where the RPE is still morphologically intact, while the number of cone numbers was relatively spared.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the histological findings.

claim: Cones of the TZ and residual rods and cones in the AZ had invariably lost their segments.
source: However, cones of the TZ and residual rods and cones in the AZ had invariably lost their segments.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the histological findings.

claim: The subretinal space above large Drusen is infiltrated with MPs.
source: Using pan- mononuclear phagocyte (MP) markers, we and others have previously shown that the subretinal space (i) above large Drusen (Lad et al., 2015; Levy et al., 2015; Sennlaub et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a cited observation from multiple studies including the authors' own work.

claim: The subretinal space within GA lesions is infiltrated with MPs.
source: Using pan- mononuclear phagocyte (MP) markers, we and others have previously shown that the subretinal space (i) above large Drusen (Lad et al., 2015; Levy et al., 2015; Sennlaub et al., 2013), (ii) within GA lesions (Combadière et al., 2007; Gupta et al., 2003; Lad et al., 2015; Sennlaub et al., 2013; Penfold et al., 2001)
evidence: This is a cited observation from multiple studies including the authors' own work.

claim: The subretinal space in the TZ of patients with GA is infiltrated with MPs.
source: Using pan- mononuclear phagocyte (MP) markers, we and others have previously shown that the subretinal space (i) above large Drusen (Lad et al., 2015; Levy et al., 2015; Sennlaub et al., 2013), (ii) within GA lesions (Combadière et al., 2007; Gupta et al., 2003; Lad et al., 2015; Sennlaub et al., 2013; Penfold et al., 2001), and (iii) in the TZ of patients with GA (Levy et al., 2015; Sennlaub et al., 2013) are infiltrated with MPs.
evidence: This is a cited observation from multiple studies including the authors' own work.

claim: Blood-born classical CD18+CCR2+Mos take part in the infiltrate above large Drusen, within GA lesions, and in the TZ.
source: We demonstrated that blood-born classical CD18+CCR2+Mos take part in the infiltrate at these three locations (Sennlaub et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a cited observation from the authors' previous work.

claim: Circulating classical Mos express high levels of CD14.
source: Circulating classical Mos also express high levels of CD14 (Geissmann et al., 2003)
evidence: This is a cited observation about monocyte marker expression.

claim: CD14 is additionally expressed by other members of the MP family.
source: Circulating classical Mos also express high levels of CD14 (Geissmann et al., 2003), which is additionally expressed by other members of the MP family (Gautier et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a cited observation about MP marker expression.

claim: CD14 is not discriminative for infiltrating Mos versus resident MPs (unlike CCR2).
source: which is additionally expressed by other members of the MP family (Gautier et al., 2012) and is therefore not discriminative for infiltrating Mos versus resident MPs (unlike CCR2).
evidence: This is an inference based on cited knowledge about marker expression patterns.

claim: Flat-mount immunohistochemistry facilitates the appreciation of cone outer segments and the detection of the smaller, dispersed MPs that are more difficult to detect on sections.
source: Flat-mount immunohistochemistry facilitates the appreciation of cone outer segments and the detection of the smaller, dispersed MPs that are more difficult to detect on sections.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the advantages of flat-mount preparations.

claim: Peanut agglutinin (PNA) stains inner and outer CS (but not cone cell bodies).
source: We used CD14 immunohistochemistry to visualize MPs, peanut agglutinin (PNA) that stains inner and outer CS (but not cone cell bodies) (Blanks and Johnson, 1984)
evidence: This is a cited observation about PNA staining specificity.

claim: Cone arrestin stains cones irrespective of the presence of CS.
source: and cone arrestin that stains cones irrespective of the presence of CS (see Figure 1).
evidence: This is a statement about cone arrestin staining specificity supported by Figure 1.

claim: In GA tissues, the retinas of the AZ adhere to Bruchs membrane in the area of RPE defects.
source: In GA tissues, the retinas of the AZ were carefully peeled from the RPE/choroid, as they adhere to Bruchs membrane in the area of RPE defects.
evidence: This is a methodological observation about tissue handling.

claim: In the TZ, the retina detaches easily from the underlying RPE, comparable to control retinas.
source: This is not the case in the TZ, where the retina detaches easily from the underlying RPE, comparable to control retinas.
evidence: This is a methodological observation about tissue handling.

claim: Subretinal CD14+MPs are only very occasionally observed in healthy age-matched donors.
source: Confocal microscopy of CD14 stained central RPE confirmed that subretinal CD14+MPs are only very occasionally observed in healthy age-matched donors (Figure 2A, CD14 white staining, RPE orange autofluorescence).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Within the AZ of patients with GA where the RPE has disappeared, CD14+MPs were numerous.
source: Within the AZ of patients with GA where the RPE has disappeared (Figure 2E right to the yellow dotted line, AZ), CD14+MPs were numerous
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2E.

claim: CD14+MPs were always observed on the autofluorescent RPE in the TZ.
source: but were also always observed on the autofluorescent RPE in the TZ (Figure 2E left to the yellow dotted line, TZ), very similar to our published results using an IBA-1 antibody (Levy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2E, consistent with previous work.

claim: The RPE expresses CD14, but to a much lesser extent compared to MPs.
source: The RPE also expresses CD14, but to a much lesser extend compared to MPs (Elner et al., 2003), which might explain why the RPE did not appear CD14-positive in our experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a cited observation with an inference about staining results.

claim: A comparative RT-PCR of CD14 in human blood-derived Mos versus human post-mortem RPE cells revealed a ten-fold stronger expression in Mo.
source: A comparative RT-PCR of CD14 in human blood-derived Mos versus human post-mortem RPE cells revealed a ten-fold stronger expression in Mo in our samples (data not shown).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from RT-PCR analysis.

claim: CD14+MCs of the central inner retina of patients with GA displayed an activated MC phenotype with shortened processes.
source: while CD14+MCs of the central inner retina of patients with GA displayed an activated MC phenotype with shortened processes (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2F.

claim: CD14+MCs stained positive for the marker IBA-1, confirming their MP nature.
source: CD14+MCs also stained positive for the marker IBA-1, confirming their MP nature (Figure 2F insets).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2F insets.

claim: In the AZ, the PNA staining was much reduced, but cone arrestin+cone cell bodies were visible in reduced numbers and their distribution was irregular.
source: In the AZ, recognizable by a severely thinned ONL and a slightly brown color in bright-field microscopy due to RPE-debris sticking to the subretinal aspect of the flat-mount, the PNA staining was much reduced, but cone arrestin+cone cell bodies were visible in reduced numbers and their distribution was irregular (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2G.

claim: In the adjacent TZ cone arrestin+ cone density was relatively spared.
source: In the adjacent TZ cone arrestin+ cone density was relatively spared (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2G.

claim: In both the AZ and TZ the typical cone arrestin+PNA+cone segment pattern had disappeared.
source: However, in both the AZ and TZ the typical cone arrestin+PNA+cone segment pattern had disappeared
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2G.

claim: At a greater distance to the atrophic zone (>1000 μm), cone arrestin and PNA immunological staining located to cone segments was indistinguishable to the pattern observed in flat-mounts from healthy donors.
source: At a greater distance to the atrophic zone (>1000 μm), cone arrestin and PNA immunological staining located to cone segments, was indistinguishable to the pattern observed in flat-mounts from healthy donors (Figure 2G inset).
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2G inset.

claim: 3D reconstruction views reveal the nearly complete loss of normal PNA+ cone segments in the transitional zone that is associated with the presence of CD14+MPs.
source: Oblique (Figure 2H) and perpendicular 3D reconstruction views (Figure 2H inset) reveal the nearly complete loss of normal PNA+ cone segments in the transitional zone that is associated with the presence of CD14+MPs.
evidence: This is a description of immunohistochemical observations shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The results confirm the loss of cone inner and outer segments adjacent to the atrophic zone where the RPE is present.
source: In summary, these results confirm the loss of cone inner and outer segments adjacent to the atrophic zone where the RPE is present that we observed in sections (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the flat-mount findings consistent with section observations.

claim: The results illustrate the close physical association of cone segment loss and CD14+Mos accumulation in the TZ.
source: They illustrate the close physical association of cone segment loss and CD14+Mos accumulation in the TZ.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the flat-mount findings.

claim: Wildtype and Cx3cr1-deficient-mouse bone marrow-derived monocytes (BMM) induce photoreceptor cell apoptosis in a monocyte/mouse retinal explant co-culture system.
source: We have previously shown that wildtype- and in particular Cx3cr1-deficient-mouse bone marrow-derived monocytes (BMM) induce photoreceptor cell apoptosis in a monocyte/ mouse retinal explant co-culture system (Sennlaub et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a cited observation from the authors' previous work.

claim: TUNEL+ nuclei in the photoreceptor cell layer of retinal explants were more numerous in the presence of Mos.
source: Apoptosis was analyzed by TUNEL staining of the retinal explants cultured without Mos (Figure 3A), or with Mos (Figure 3B). TUNEL+ nuclei in the photoreceptor cell layer of retinal explants were more numerous in the presence of Mos.
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: The TUNEL+ nuclei of the ONL were positive for rhodopsin and not located at proximity to the inner segments, where cone nuclei are located.
source: Double-immunological labeling for rhodopsin and TUNEL on sections prepared from the retinal explants revealed that the TUNEL+ nuclei of the ONL were positive for rhodopsin (Figure 3C inset) and not located at proximity to the inner segments, where cone nuclei are located (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Apoptosis was only observed in a minority of rods in these short-term co-cultures.
source: Apoptosis was only observed in a minority of rods in these short-term co-cultures and rhodopsin+rod segments were unremarkable in the culture condition (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Rhodopsin+rod segments were unremarkable in the culture condition.
source: Apoptosis was only observed in a minority of rods in these short-term co-cultures and rhodopsin+rod segments were unremarkable in the culture condition (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Quantification of TUNEL+ nuclei/mm on 8 explants per group revealed a significant increase in TUNEL+ photoreceptors in co-culture with hMos compared to retinal explants cultured without hMos.
source: Quantification of TUNEL+ nuclei/mm on 8 explants per group revealed a significant increase in TUNEL+ photoreceptors in co-culture with hMos compared to retinal explants cultured without hMos (Figure 3D)
evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Quantification of cone arrestin+PNA+ cones revealed no influence of the presence of hMos on the number of cones after 18 hr of culture.
source: Quantification of cone arrestin+PNA+ cones (Figure 3G) revealed no influence of the presence of hMos on the number of cones after 18 hr of culture.
evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The PNA-staining in hMo-exposed retinal flat-mounts appeared punctuated and the typical elongated shape of mouse PNA+CS staining in retinas cultured without Mos had disappeared.
source: However, the PNA-staining in hMo-exposed retinal flat-mounts appeared punctuated and the typical elongated shape of mouse PNA+CS staining in retinas cultured without Mos had disappeared (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is a qualitative experimental observation shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: 3D reconstruction views reveal the near complete loss of PNA+CS in the hMo exposed explants.
source: Oblique and perpendicular 3D reconstruction views of confocal microscopy Z-stacks of explant mono-cultures (Figure 3H), or co-culture with hMos (Figure 3I) reveals the near complete loss of PNA+CS in the hMo exposed explants.
evidence: This is a qualitative experimental observation shown in Figures 3H and 3I.

claim: Arrestin staining revealed a severe shortening of arrestin+CS in the co-culture condition compared to controls.
source: Similarly, arrestin staining revealed a severe shortening of arrestin+CS in the co-culture condition compared to controls (Figure 3H and I insets).
evidence: This is a qualitative experimental observation shown in Figure 3H and I insets.

claim: Quantification of PNA+ volume in retinal explants co-cultured with increasing numbers of hMo confirms a severe, significant reduction in PNA+CS volume as a function of hMos numbers.
source: Quantification of PNA+ volume (quantitated on the whole Z-stack, divided by the number of cones) in retinal explants co-cultured with increasing numbers of hMo confirms numerically a severe, significant reduction in PNA+CS volume as a function of hMos numbers (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Mouse retinal explants co-cultured with Cx3cr1-deficient-mouse BMMs revealed a similar, severe reduction in CS volume.
source: To evaluate eventual artifacts due to interspecies incompatibilities we next quantified PNA+CS volumes of mouse retinal explants that we co-cultured for 18 hr with 100 000 Cx3cr1-deficient-mouse BMMs (which induces rod apoptosis similar to hMos [Sennlaub et al., 2013]). Our results revealed a similar, severe reduction in CS volume (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation shown in Figure 3K.
